question: How do I create a page whose URL contains a variable part, like a blog post slug?
answer: Wrap a folder name in square brackets, e.g. app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx; the value is passed to the page in the params prop.

question: After a Server Action changes data, how do I make the page show the updated data?
answer: Call revalidatePath or revalidateTag (or updateTag) inside the Server Function after the mutation.

question: How can every page title automatically include the site name as a suffix?
answer: Set title.template in the root layout metadata, e.g. '%s | Acme'; child segments that set a title are inserted into %s, and title.default is the fallback.

question: How can I show a skeleton while a route is fetching its data?
answer: Add a loading.js file to the route segment; Next.js wraps the page in a React Suspense boundary and shows it as the fallback.

question: How do I show a fallback UI when a part of the app throws an unexpected runtime error?
answer: Add an error.js file (a Client Component) to the segment; it acts as an error boundary for its children and receives the error and a way to retry.

question: How do I customize the page shown when a URL does not exist in the App Router?
answer: Create a not-found.js file; it renders when notFound() is called in the segment, and the root app/not-found.js also handles unmatched URLs.

question: How do I build a JSON API endpoint inside the app directory?
answer: Create a route.ts file and export functions named after HTTP methods (GET, POST, ...) that receive a Request and return a Response.

question: What happened to middleware in Next.js 16?
answer: The middleware file convention is deprecated and renamed to proxy (proxy.ts); it still runs code on the server before a request completes.

question: How do I make a component run in the browser so it can use useState and onClick?
answer: Add the 'use client' directive at the top of the file, before any imports; it marks the entry point of a Client Component tree.

question: How do I let the Image component load pictures hosted on another domain?
answer: Pass a URL as src, provide width and height manually, and allow the host with images.remotePatterns in next.config.

question: How do I use a Google Font without sending requests to Google from the browser?
answer: Import it from next/font/google; Next.js self-hosts it as a static asset served from your own domain.

question: How do I stop a link in the footer from being prefetched?
answer: Pass prefetch={false} to the Link component.

question: How do I send the user to a different URL from a Server Component?
answer: Call redirect() from next/navigation (or permanentRedirect for a permanent one).

question: How do I read a cookie value in a Server Component?
answer: Await cookies() from next/headers and call .get(name); cookies is async and read-only in Server Components.

question: How do I prerender every blog post page at build time?
answer: Export generateStaticParams from the dynamic route segment, returning the list of params to build.

question: How can one layout render two independent sections, like team and analytics, at the same time?
answer: Use parallel routes: named slots in @folder folders that are passed to the shared layout as props.

question: How do I open a photo in a modal while keeping a shareable URL for it?
answer: Combine intercepting routes ((.) folder convention) with parallel routes so the route renders in a modal on navigation and as a full page on direct load.

question: How can I group routes into folders without the folder name showing up in the URL?
answer: Wrap the folder name in parentheses, e.g. (marketing); route groups are omitted from the URL path.

question: Why is my environment variable undefined in client-side code?
answer: Only variables prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_ are inlined into the browser bundle at build time; others exist only in the Node.js environment.

question: How do I produce a minimal build to run in a Docker container?
answer: Set output: 'standalone' in next.config; it creates .next/standalone with only the needed files, deployable without node_modules.

question: How do I serve the whole app under a sub-path like /docs?
answer: Set basePath: '/docs' in next.config.

question: How do I forward /api requests to another backend without changing the URL the user sees?
answer: Add rewrites in next.config mapping the source path to the external destination.

question: Why should a component that reads useSearchParams be wrapped in Suspense?
answer: On a prerendered route, useSearchParams makes the tree up to the nearest Suspense boundary render on the client, so the rest of the route can still be prerendered.

question: How do I navigate to another page from a button click handler?
answer: In a Client Component, use useRouter from next/navigation and call router.push(href).

question: How do I handle a form submission on the server without writing an API endpoint?
answer: Pass a Server Function (a 'use server' async function) to the form's action prop; it receives the FormData.

question: How do I control how long a cached function stays fresh?
answer: Call cacheLife (e.g. cacheLife('hours')) inside a function or component that uses the 'use cache' directive.

question: How can editors preview unpublished content from a headless CMS?
answer: Use Draft Mode: a Route Handler enables it (setting a cookie) and pages render draft content at request time while it is on.

question: How do I generate the image shown when a page is shared on social media?
answer: Add an opengraph-image file (static image or code that returns an ImageResponse) to the route segment.

question: How do I give search engines a list of all my URLs?
answer: Add app/sitemap.xml, or app/sitemap.ts exporting a function that returns the list of URLs.

question: Where do I put code that must run once when the server starts, such as setting up monitoring?
answer: In instrumentation.ts at the project root (or src), exporting a register function that runs once when a server instance starts.

question: How can TypeScript catch typos in the href of my links?
answer: Enable typedRoutes in next.config (now stable, no longer experimental) to get statically typed links.

question: In the Pages Router, how do I fetch fresh data on every request?
answer: Export getServerSideProps from the page; it runs on the server for each request and passes props to the page.

question: In the Pages Router, how do I rebuild a static page in the background at most once per minute?
answer: Return revalidate: 60 from getStaticProps (Incremental Static Regeneration).

question: How do I create an API endpoint with the Pages Router?
answer: Add a file under pages/api; it exports a default handler (req, res) and is a server-only endpoint.

question: In the Pages Router, where do I add global CSS and a layout shared by every page?
answer: In a custom App: pages/_app.js, whose component wraps every page.

question: How do I run logging or analytics after the response has already been sent?
answer: Use after() from next/server to schedule a callback that runs once the response (or prerender) is finished.

question: How do I load a third-party script only when the browser is idle?
answer: Use the Script component with strategy="lazyOnload".

question: How do I set the title and description of a page in the App Router?
answer: Export a metadata object (or a generateMetadata function) from layout.js or page.js.

question: What is the difference between updateTag and revalidateTag?
answer: updateTag works only in Server Actions and makes the next request wait for fresh data (read-your-own-writes); revalidateTag also works in Route Handlers and, with profile 'max', serves stale data while refreshing in the background.

question: Can I keep using a webpack loader such as an SVG loader with Turbopack?
answer: Yes, many webpack loaders work: configure them under turbopack.rules in next.config. Only a subset of the loader API is supported and loaders must return JavaScript.
